jobs.title: Engineering Manager - Solutions Engineering
jobs.jd_full:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

We want to transform the world of software operations by enabling true model-driven operations via next-generation infrastructure-as-code. This will allow companies to run very efficient bare-metal operations for high-performance computing, private cloud, data lakes, AI/ML, and analytics. We need to invent some new technology, and we need to build some new products; we are therefore looking for someone who can lead and inspire a regional software engineering team to fulfill this initiative.

The Solutions Engineering team works in close collaboration with our managed infrastructure operations team, which runs many private OpenStack clouds and Kubernetes clusters for customers around the world. This enables us to improve our infra-as-code products based on our own real experience, mirroring that of our users and customers. We work in Python, creating open-source automation capabilities that simplify operations for anybody, anywhere, who is building on Ubuntu.

Most of the team's work involves pure Python software development focused on enabling true DevOps workflows. We strive for high quality in both design, documentation, tests, and performance as we enhance operations code packages and Ubuntu itself in order to ensure our platform is the easiest, most robust, and best performing for driving your infrastructure.

As an Engineering Manager, your primary responsibility is to the people you lead and support: ensuring that they are growing as engineers, doing valuable work, and finding satisfaction in their career at Canonical. About Us

Chorus Innovations is a fast-growing healthcare technology company with an adaptive platform as a service (PaaS) that enables the rapid development of mobile, desktop, text messaging and interactive voice applications. Chorus’ platform currently powers transformative healthcare, biomedical research and community health projects across institutions and public health agencies nationwide. We believe every community should have world-class health technology so they can thrive.

Our mission is to improve the lives of people and communities by democratizing technology development in health and research.

About the Role

As a Lead Product Manager, you will own the vision, strategy, and evolution of key product lines within the Chorus platform , and you’ll partner with the VP, Product on an execution strategy. You will translate market needs, client patterns, and platform capabilities into clear product direction, balancing strategic foresight with the pragmatism needed to drive outcomes in a complex healthcare ecosystem.

You will work at the intersection of R&D, Delivery, and Go-To-Market, setting the direction for each product area and transforming ambiguous, broad objectives into clear, actionable project roadmaps that allow platform reuse, and unlock scalable growth. You’ll define problems deeply, synthesize insights from users, clinical experts, research, and stakeholders, and convert them into product requirements, sequencing, and standards — then stay close enough to the work to course-correct in real time.

As a senior leader on the Product team, you will set the bar for clarity, prioritization, and measurable impact. You will shape product narratives, drive cross-functional alignment, and build the artifacts (requirements, stories, templates, and playbooks) that let Delivery teams and external partners move faster with higher quality. jobs.jd_full:
We’re building the AI-powered future of maintenance.

UpKeep is on a mission to reinvent how the physical world runs—starting with the frontline teams who maintain it. We’re the creators of the world’s first AI-first CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System), equipping technicians and facilities teams with automation, machine learning, and predictive insights that drive operational speed, safety, and efficiency.

What started as a garage-built prototype is now a fast-scaling SaaS company, backed by Insight Partners, Emergence Capital, and Y Combinator. Over 4,000 companies—including Shell, Yamaha, Unilever, and Marriott—run on UpKeep to modernize their asset operations. We’re leading the $30B category shift toward Asset Operations Management, where uptime, intelligence, and AI converge.

Why join us:

  • Own the AI-first transformation of an entire industry. Every feature we ship leverages AI—from predictive work orders to sensor-driven automations. You’re not just iterating—you’re pioneering how data reshapes physical operations.

  • Real traction, real scale. Recognized as Gartner’s #1 Facility Management solution and G2’s top-rated CMMS, we’ve earned market leadership through product, not puff.

  • A company where builders thrive. We move fast, optimize for outcomes, and give high-agency operators the autonomy to ship big things. Our culture rewards bold thinking, not bureaucracy.

  • Global team, local energy. With 100+ employees across the world, we support remote-first work with deep investment in our LA HQ—where certain roles and leadership converge for rapid innovation.

  • Equity and upside, not just a paycheck. Competitive comp, meaningful ownership, and benefits that support your health, focus, and long-term growth.

If you’re driven by impact, energized by AI, and hungry to transform a legacy industry—we’re hiring!

POSITION SUMMARY

As Director, Revenue Strategy & Operations, you will build the analytical and AI infrastructure that tells us what is happening in the funnel, why it is happening, what Sales and Marketing should do about it, and where Finance should allocate resources across the GTM function.

This is a hands-on role leading a lean RevOps function that supports Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance. It is centered on full-funnel growth and revenue analytics — understanding the drivers of new business, retention, expansion, pipeline, conversion, and productivity, and translating those insights into clear decisions about where the company should focus. Handed a pipeline export, your instinct should be to find the problem, and to find what is working well enough to scale.

This role reports to the CFO. You will lead and develop the RevOps team, including the Deal Desk Manager and Salesforce Administrator, and work in dotted-line partnership with the Sales Operations Manager, GTM Engineering, and Marketing Operations. This is not a role for someone who manages through layers or operates exclusively at the strategic level — you should be comfortable getting into the data, inspecting the funnel, building the analyses and models yourself, and sitting down with functional leaders to solve problems.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the weekly inspection of pipeline creation, lead flow, funnel conversion, and rep-level productivity, and turn each week’s findings into a short, specific list of actions for Sales and Marketing leadership.
  • Diagnose where the funnel is breaking and where it is outperforming, and make sure both get acted on.
  • Assess opportunity and pipeline quality directly, rather than taking stage and amount at face value.
  • Use AI to inspect pipeline at scale — opportunity quality, deal risk, and forecast credibility — rather than sampling manually.
  • Build AI-driven workflows for account prioritization, buying-signal detection, and weekly GTM inspection, replacing recurring manual analysis with automated reporting that leadership can trust.
  • Partner with GTM Engineering and functional leaders to identify and implement high-value AI use cases.
  • Deliver end-to-end visibility from lead generation through new business, onboarding, retention, expansion, and churn, including the analytical view of GRR, NRR, churn, and expansion tied back to acquisition source, segment, and deal characteristics.
  • Analyze conversion, velocity, pipeline health, cohort and segment performance, and revenue leakage; identify what our best customers and closed-won deals have in common and sharpen ICP, targeting, and segmentation around it.
  • Own the analytical framework for GTM capacity planning — headcount, productivity, quota capacity, pipeline requirements, and segment opportunity — and model the expected return from incremental GTM headcount, programs, and channels in partnership with Finance on annual planning.
  • Pressure-test forecast assumptions and surface leading indicators before they show up in reported results, partnering with the Sales Operations Manager, who owns the weekly forecast process, deal-level scrutiny, and sales operating cadence.
  • Own the GTM performance narrative for executive leadership and the Board, anticipating the questions before they are asked.
  • Set priorities and requirements for core GTM systems, data architecture, and reporting, and govern GTM definitions, metrics, and data quality so that Salesforce and other systems produce reliable, decision-useful data.

EXPERIENCE

  • 6–10+ years across Sales Strategy, Sales Operations, GTM Strategy, Revenue Analytics, Revenue Intelligence, Revenue Operations, or FP&A
  • A career built through Sales Strategy, Sales Ops, Marketing Ops, or GTM Strategy, rather than one centered primarily on Salesforce administration and systems ownership
  • Experience at high-growth SaaS companies in the ~$30M–$150M ARR range, where you personally pulled the data, built the model, and worked directly in the CRM
  • Proven ability to diagnose performance problems independently — and equally, to spot what is working and build the case for scaling it
  • Bachelor’s Degree with equivalent experience a plus

KNOWLEDGE

  • Deep, practical AI experience — hands-on building, not familiarity with AI tools for drafting and content generation
  • Hands-on with the modern GTM stack: Salesforce, Gong, Clay, enrichment and intent data, SQL, dbt, or BI tools
  • Strong full-funnel analytics: pipeline, conversion, segmentation, retention, expansion, cohort analysis, and capacity modeling
  • Strong Excel/Google Sheets modeling skills; SQL, BI, or data warehouse experience is a plus
  • Exposure to Salesforce Revenue Cloud / CPQ or similar quote-to-cash systems is preferred; this is not a Salesforce implementation role, and you will not be the day-to-day administrator
  • Root-cause diagnosis across Marketing, BDR, Sales, and Customer Success — demand, qualification, process, capacity, productivity, or execution
  • Ability to communicate complex analytical findings clearly to executives and functional leaders
  • Builder mentality: inquisitive, high-energy, low-ego, and comfortable working in a small team and directly in the details

DESIRED BEHAVIORS

  • Receptive to change – is flexible. Seeks and adopts improved approaches and processes.
  • Initiates action – is results oriented, takes responsibility for actions and outcomes. Meets commitments and strives for high performance.
  • Manages the workload - makes timely decisions, prioritizes effectively, solves problems, monitors results and takes remedial action where necessary.
  • Technically proficient – knows the role and has a solid familiarity with tasks and responsibilities.
  • Takes responsibility for own learning - knows personal strengths and recognizes development needs. Is open to feedback and always seeks to learn.
  • Communicates ideas – strong facilitation and written communication, proposes a way forward. Listens to views of colleagues and takes in diverse perspectives.
  • Works collaboratively – shares information, fosters teamwork and contributes to a positive work environment where people want to come to work.
  • Display ethical character and competence - acts with integrity and intent, is accountable for own actions, behaves according to the company values.
  • Act as a good citizen of UpKeep.

COMPENSATION

This role will receive a competitive base salary + benefits. A variety of factors are considered when determining someone’s compensation–including a candidate’s professional background, experience, and location. Final offer amounts may vary from the amounts listed below.

The pay range for this role is $210,000 - $225,000.

Company History & Product:

UpKeep started in a garage, where our founder Ryan taught himself to code and built the first mobile-first maintenance app. The idea was simple but powerful: put modern software in the hands of frontline technicians—and transform how maintenance gets done.

Today, UpKeep is the leading cloud-native Asset Operations Management platform, serving over 4,000 businesses worldwide across manufacturing, utilities, healthcare, and beyond. Our Industrial IoT and AI-first software helps maintenance and facilities teams streamline work, predict failures, and act faster—with real-time insights and automation at their fingertips.

We’re building for the deskless workforce—the essential workers who keep our physical world running—and arming them with the tools they deserve.  In a world re-shoring manufacturing, accelerating automation, and embracing AI at scale, we’re riding the next macro wave—and leading the transformation of legacy maintenance into intelligent operations.

Backed by $50 million from Insight Partners, Emergence Capital, Mucker, and Y Combinator,we’re not just building software.  We’re defining a new category for the built world.

jobs.jd_full:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Deployment Project Manager to join our team.

Position Description

The Deployment Project Manager is a pivotal, execution-focused role responsible for advancing Oklo’s mission to deliver clean, affordable, and reliable energy. This individual owns the end-to-end delivery of one or more highly complex powerhouse projects, from design integration and site development through construction, startup, commissioning, and turnover to operations.

These multi-year, non-recurring projects include significant first-of-a-kind scope, substantial commercial value, evolving risks, and complex dependencies across internal teams, external partners, regulators, and other key stakeholders. The Deployment Project Manager serves as the central point of coordination, driving integrated planning, decision-making, risk management, and clear communication among project teams, executive leadership, and external parties. Success in this role requires a strategic and hands-on leader with a startup mindset - someone who can bring structure to ambiguity, operate effectively in a resource-constrained environment, and maintain momentum, accountability, and alignment throughout the full project lifecycle.

Location: Remote, with 25%–40% travel required

Specific responsibilities may include:

  • Lead end-to-end execution of powerhouse facility deployments from design through startup and turnover to operations.
  • Support and maintain integrated project plans, schedules, milestones, and execution tools to monitor progress and drive delivery.
  • Identify, manage, and escalate risks, issues, dependencies, and changes to protect critical path, licensing, regulatory, and commercial objectives.
  • Lead project governance routines, including status reviews, stage-gate reviews, and executive reporting.
  • Manage project scope, risks, issues, and dependencies while proactively identifying and implementing mitigation strategies.
  • Communicate project status, recommendations, and strategic insights to stakeholders ranging from project teams to executive leadership.
  • Support permitting, licensing, facility modifications, equipment installations, and infrastructure upgrade projects.
  • Oversee contractor performance, procurement activities, material sourcing, and project deliverables.
  • Serve as the primary point of coordination among internal teams, customers, contractors, vendors, and other external stakeholders.
  • Contribute to technical strategy, execution planning, and continuous improvement initiatives that support organizational goals.
  • Ensure projects are executed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with applicable quality, regulatory, and operational requirements.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Project Management, Construction Management, Nuclear Engineering, Business, or a related technical discipline.
  • Minimum of 5 years of project management experience leading complex technical, engineering, construction, manufacturing, or operational projects.
  • Experience managing project scope, schedules, budgets, risks, milestones, and cross-functional dependencies.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead teams, resolve blockers, and communicate effectively with technical and business stakeholders.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to operate with agility and sound judgment in a fast-moving, evolving organization.
  • Proficiency with project planning, scheduling, and collaboration tools.

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Nuclear experience in design, construction, commissioning, or operations
  • PMP certification is strongly preferred.
  • Experience managing contractor-driven projects, capital projects, facility upgrades, or equipment installation efforts.
  • Familiarity with quality assurance, configuration management, permitting, or regulatory compliance processes.

Competencies

We are looking for a Deployment Project Manager that is:

  • Passionate about advancing the deployment of next-generation powerhouse facilities
  • Creative when pursuing tasks in resource constrained environments
  • You’re not afraid to roll up your sleeves and deliver
  • You see how the pieces connect and can manage interfaces
  • You turn ambiguity into momentum
  • Eager to work on a dynamic team, receive constructive feedback, and grow with us
  • An active and effective communicator of priorities
  • Able to recognize, accept, and manage risk
  • Passionate about Oklo’s mission to design and deploy advanced fission power plants to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy
  • Willing to think differently and do things in new ways
  • Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment
  • Excited to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about the problems they are solving, while not leaning only on what has been done before

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren’t driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don’t need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

About Oklo travel requirements:

Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

About Oklo compensation:

Salary: $100,000-$160,000

Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, bonuses, competitive pay, 401(k), health insurance (with employer contribution), HSA, FSA, flexible work hours, wellness credits, and other benefits.

This position may involve access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Only applicants who meet the definition of a U.S. person under applicable laws may be eligible.

About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

#CHOP: Oklo’s Values

Collaboration: We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.

Humility: We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.

Ownership: We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through  to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.

Pathfinding: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.

jobs.title: Principal Program Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Assured is on a mission to modernize insurance. Claims processing (i.e. should we pay this claim?), while often overlooked, is the foundation of the entire industry. It’s currently highly manual, involving phone calls, faxes, and gut instinct, costing tens of billions of dollars a year. We can do better.

At Assured, we provide large insurers with the software solutions they need to win in a modern, technology-driven world. From self-service claim-filing software to backend fraud detection, we’re the engine that powers claims processing for some of the largest insurers in the world.

The challenges we face are deep and diverse, from creating digital experiences that provide comfort and clarity to claimants at their most stressed and vulnerable to orchestrating large-scale ML-driven decision-making on billions of dollars of claims payments, life at Assured is dynamic, collaborative, and rewarding.

We’re looking for an experienced Principal Program Manager to join our Client Engagement team.

In this role, you’ll help turn complex client priorities into clear, executable programs across Client Engagement, Product, Engineering, and client stakeholders. You’ll own the operating rhythm for high-stakes client initiatives, from kickoff and scoping through launch, adoption, and long-term success.

This is a role for someone who can bring structure to ambiguity, keep cross-functional work moving, and build trust with both internal teams and enterprise customers.

P&C insurance industry experience is a strong plus, but not required. What matters most is the ability to learn the domain quickly and build credibility with enterprise clients.

Some of the Work You’ll Own:

🔗 Turn client needs into clear execution plans. Sit between Product, Engineering, and client stakeholders to translate client priorities into scoped initiatives, owners, timelines, risks, and next steps.

🚀 Drive high-stakes carrier initiatives from kickoff to launch. Own the operating plan for client-facing projects, including dependencies, decision points, launch readiness, stakeholder alignment, and the many details that determine whether a rollout feels controlled or chaotic.

📋 Build the Client Engagement operating muscle. Create the intake, tracking, status, and escalation rhythms that help Client Engagement manage carrier work consistently as Assured scales.

🧭 Make risks and tradeoffs visible early. When timelines shift, scope expands, or dependencies get stuck, surface the issue clearly, frame the options, and help the right people make the right call before it becomes a client-facing fire drill.

🗣️ Be the translator across clients and internal teams. Turn carrier feedback, asks, and concerns into clear internal action. Turn Product and Engineering constraints into client-ready explanations that build confidence instead of confusion.

🔍 Find patterns across client work. Notice when multiple carriers are asking for the same thing, running into the same friction, or needing the same support, and help turn those patterns into better processes, product improvements, or scalable client programs.

⏱️ Keep multiple concurrent initiatives balanced and honest. Manage the mechanics that keep complex work moving, including RAID logs, dependency mapping, launch plans, follow-ups, status reporting, and critical path management, without adding process for process’s sake.

How You’ll Make an Impact:

🎯 Improve confidence in client delivery. Help Assured give enterprise clients clearer visibility, tighter execution, and more predictable launches across complex initiatives. You’ll build trust by being organized, precise, and honest about what is known, unknown, and changing.

🔍 Keep everyone aligned without meeting overload. Build clear status updates, trackers, launch plans, and decision logs so leadership, Client Engagement, Product, Engineering, and client stakeholders can understand where things stand without needing another meeting just to find the answer.

⚡ Use AI to move faster. Use tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and similar platforms to draft project plans, synthesize client feedback, maintain documentation, identify risks, and keep work moving without letting coordination consume the week.

📈 Help scale Client Engagement. As Assured grows, Client Engagement needs better systems for managing client commitments, launches, escalations, and cross-functional work. You’ll help build the operating model that lets the team scale without losing the high-touch client experience.

You’ll Probably Thrive Here If You:

🏗️ Have deep program management experience. You’ve led complex, cross-functional work with real stakeholder pressure, shifting timelines, ambiguous requirements, and external customers in the mix. You know how to create structure, drive alignment, and keep teams moving when the path is not perfectly defined.

💬 Are client-facing and internally rigorous. You can communicate clearly with client stakeholders, then turn around and drive internal follow-through with the right level of detail.

🛠️ Are comfortable being technical-adjacent. You don’t need to write code, but you need to understand product and engineering constraints well enough to ask good questions, scope honestly, and avoid hand-wavy commitments.

🧭 Can operate without waiting for perfect clarity. You know how to create structure when the path is still forming. You can identify what matters, what’s blocked, who owns what, and what decision needs to happen next.

⚖️ Balance urgency with discipline. You move quickly, but you don’t skip the basics: owners, dates, risks, dependencies, decisions, and follow-up.

🗣️ Lead through influence. You know how to get people moving together by being clear, trusted, and relentlessly organized.

🔄 Learn the domain fast. Prior insurance experience is helpful, but curiosity and speed of learning matter more. You should be able to quickly understand claims workflows, carrier operations, product behavior, and the client context behind each request.
